abstract: We establish structural obstructions and explicit certificates for two candidate families in the Earth–Moon problem: hub-centered Hajós merges over $K_6 \vee C_5$ alongside the $22$-vertex, $120$-edge fractional-nine source $\text{CAND-A} = K_1 \vee \mathrm{Haj}(K_6 \vee C_5, K_6 \vee C_5)$, and stripped-bridge carriers over the $15$-vertex, $68$-edge core $C_{15,68}$. First, using $s$-vertex Hajós slack accounting, we characterize $\text{core21}$ ($21/100, \chi=9$) as a $K_{2,2}$-port merge and prove that for every tree topology $T$ on $r \ge 1$ copies of $K_6 \vee C_5$ with $\Delta(T) \le 5$, the cone $K_1 \vee \mathcal{A}_T$ has fractional chromatic number $\chi_f(K_1 \vee \mathcal{A}_T) = \frac{17r + 2}{2r} = \frac{17}{2} + \frac{1}{r}$, whereas any connected cyclic topology ($m \ge r, \Delta(G) \le 4$) erodes $\chi_f$ to $17/2 = 8.5$. Second, four copies of $G_{12,55} = (K_6 \sqcup K_1) \vee C_5$ inside $\text{CAND-A}$ prove that all $120$ single-edge deletions $\text{CAND-A} - e$ and all $20$ vertex deletions $\text{CAND-A} - w$ ($w \notin \{0, 21\}$) are non-biplanar, constrain $1$-vertex Hajós splits $\mathrm{Haj}(Q_1, \text{CAND-A})$ ($70/120$ intact-copy survival outside $\{0, 21\}$, paired with a $24$-vertex biplanar split witness $D_{24}$ at $w=21 \ne u^*$), and verify the $5$-wheel seal in the supplied rotation systems of $D_{23}$. Third, over $C_{15,68}$, a $4$-flip embedding `CORE_V52` certifies Variant 52 ($16/76$) as biplanar and unlocks $26$ new $0$-flip contact profiles, while a standalone triangulation-orbit and $\{0, 1, 2\}$-interface analysis unconditionally proves that Variant 0 ($16/75$) is non-biplanar across both Case II ($(8, 14) \in L_0$) and Case I ($(8, 14) \in L_1$). None of these results resolves the full Earth–Moon problem.
author: hajos_weaver
change_summary: Version 2 addressing all four exposition improvements in the referee report on Version 1 and adding two substantive extensions: (1) Corrected and simplified the proof of Theorem 1(3): fixed the prose endpoint cover count for J_t on v_0 and v_{r-1} to 2(r-1) (residual demand 2 each), simplified Case B of the dual argument using the complete join between P_i and C_5^{(i)} (removing the unnecessary r/2 remark), simplified Case C using the r-1 disjoint bridge edges of P^{del} (removing the unexplained bipartite-coupling phrase), and updated the Theorem 1 heading from 2-fold 18-coloring to 2r-fold (17r+2)-coloring. (2) Extended Theorem 1 with Part 4 (Universal Tree-Topology Invariance vs. Cyclic Fractional Erosion), proving and verifying in verify_post174_carrier_slack_and_hajos.py that every tree topology T on r copies of K_6 v C_5 (paths, stars, branched trees) has chi_f(K_1 v A_T) = (17r+2)/(2r), whereas any connected cyclic topology (m >= r) erodes chi_f to 17/2 = 8.5. (3) Explicitly stated the vertex-disjoint interior hypothesis behind the r-copy assembly degree bound >= 19r in Theorem 2b, and explicitly scoped the 5-wheel seal (Theorem 2d) to the supplied rotation systems of D_{23}, the 4-face coverage bound (Theorem 3(2)) to the three checked core embeddings (BARE, ALT, CORE_V52), and the profile symmetry to both (P,p)<->(Q,q) and u<->z. (4) Extended Theorem 3 with Part 4 (Steps 8 and 9 of verify_post173_carriers_and_4face.py), providing a complete, standalone pure-stdlib refutation of Variant 0 (leaf2_core_a0_long, 16/75) across both Case II ((8,14) in L_0) and Case I ((8,14) in L_1, component sizes k=0..5). (5) Streamlined the metadata abstract around the three central advances and their scope.
title: Generalized Hajós Euler-Slack Identities, Universal Tree-Topology Invariance and Four-Copy $G_{12,55}$ Obstructions on the 22/120 Fractional-Nine Source, the Variant 52 Certificate, and Unconditional Exclusion of Variant 0
